subject: Supplier portal invite redirecting to wrong tenant / login failing
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@eastwoodmfg.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Can't accept supplier invite — redirects me to another tenant (302)

Hi Markus,

We're trying to finish the onboarding forms for Eastwood Manufacturing but when I click the supplier invite link (Ariba) it briefly loads and then redirects me to https://portal.redwood.com/tenant/northridge-procure and shows a login error page (HTTP 302 -> 403). Attached is a screenshot of the redirect (screenshot-302.png).

We tried in Chrome and Edge, cleared cookies, and still end up at the other tenant. Our IT team (cc'd) thinks there might be a proxy or header rewrite on their side, but the link itself looks correct in the email. We can't complete W-9 / bank info because we never land on the Eastwood tenant.

Can you please advise? This is blocking our first PO.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Procurement Lead, Eastwood Manufacturing
sam.patel@eastwoodmfg.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Can't accept supplier invite — redirects me to another tenant (302)

Thanks for the heads-up, Sam — sorry for the disruption.

Quick questions to help triage:
- Can you forward the original invite email (raw headers) or save and send the browser network trace?
- Does the redirect happen immediately after clicking, or do you briefly see the acceptance page?
- Can you try using an incognito window (to rule out cookies/extensions) and paste the final redirect URL?

Monica / Ben — looping you in. My initial hypothesis is that RelayState / tenant hint in the query string is being dropped or rewritten by a proxy somewhere in the path. If we can get the request/response headers from Sam's browser (or the attached portal-access-headers.txt if they can grab it), we should be able to see whether our tenant query param is being removed.

Sam — we'll get this looked at and share a manual activation link if we need to bypass the invite flow while we investigate.

—Markus
Director, GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Can't accept supplier invite — redirects me to another tenant (302)

Ben — forwarding Sam's report. Attached (portal-access-headers.txt) are the headers Sam captured from their browser (they saved it for us).

Preliminary notes from my side:
- The original invite link includes a query string with a tenant hint and RelayState: 
  /accept?invite=abcd1234&relayState=tenant:eastwood-mfg
- The captured request arriving at our edge (see logs) shows the relayState missing and a Referer header replaced with a sanitized corporate proxy URL.
- This smells like a reverse-proxy or corporate DLP that strips or normalizes query parameters (particularly anything with a colon). If RelayState is lost, the session routing goes to default tenant, which explains the northridge redirect.

Can you check:
1) Our edge routing rules for empty RelayState handling — do we fallback to tenant 'northridge-procure' in that case?
2) Any recent rewrites at the CDN/proxy layer that touch query strings or header normalization rules?

I've cc'd Sam so they can respond to any quick asks. If you want I can request a temporary manual activation link for Eastwood while we investigate.

Monica
Onboarding Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@eastwoodmfg.com>, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Can't accept supplier invite — redirects me to another tenant (302)

Hi Sam — thanks for the detailed repro and the header dump. We dug into the edge logs and the CDN config. Summary and immediate action: 

Findings:
- The invite link's RelayState was being passed as part of the query string with a colon-based hint (relayState=tenant:eastwood-mfg). Some corporate proxies (and our legacy query-normalizer) interpret the colon as an unsafe character and strip the parameter entirely.
- When RelayState is missing we fall back to a default tenant resolution logic which in your case maps to 'northridge-procure' (this is a known fallback; engineer ticket created).

Short-term workaround (please try these in order):
1) Open this direct activation link (temporary, expires in 48 hours): https://portal.redwood.com/accept/manual/ACT-9b7f4e2d?tenant=eastwood-mfg — this bypasses RelayState and forces the tenant.
2) If that fails, try adding the tenant param manually to the invite link you received by appending &tenant=eastwood-mfg.
3) Try in an incognito window (some proxies behave differently for new sessions).

I've attached a trimmed log snippet showing the missing relayState at our edge for your requests (see portal-access-headers.txt). Engineering will push a config to accept tenant hints via an alternate query param (tenant=) as a more robust fix; I've filed JIRA-INFR-8421 and set priority P2.

Can you confirm whether the manual link works? If it does, we'll mark this as resolved for the PO and keep you posted on the config rollout.

Apologies for the friction — appreciate the quick heads-up.

—Ben
Sr. Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@eastwoodmfg.com>

Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, it@eastwoodmfg.com

Ben / team — confirmed: the manual activation link worked and I'm now seeing the Eastwood onboarding form. I completed the W-9 and bank info and submitted the profile.

Thank you for the fast turnaround and the clear workaround. Our IT team will still review the proxy behavior on our side, but please keep me posted on JIRA-INFR-8421 and an ETA for a permanent fix, since we have more suppliers who might hit this.

—Sam
Procurement Lead, Eastwood Manufacturing
